title: regional-api-capacity-projections-gpu-mix-q1-2026
content:
Summary:
This working sheet estimates Q1 peak load for the Hosted API across three primary regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west), converts request forecasts to tokens/sec, and translates token demand into GPU capacity plans by model class and GPU family. Purpose is to define committed (Reserved/Dedicated) capacity targets and runbook headroom margins for predictable latency under P95 SLOs.

Key takeaways (high level):
- Projected global peak tokens/sec (baseline scenario): 360,000 tokens/sec.
- Recommended committed capacity (conservative): 140 A10G-equivalent GPUs distributed regionally (see allocation table).
- Target operational utilization: 65% average with 25% short-term burst headroom and 10% buffer for maintenance/fallback.
- Primary risk: model mix shifts toward 70B-class -> GPU requirement increases ~3x for affected routes.

Assumptions (inputs):
- Traffic windows: daily peak between 16:00-18:00 UTC, multi-minute bursts up to 3x baseline peak.
- Avg tokens/request by route: chat-interactive=180 tokens, generation-long=640 tokens, embedding=8 tokens (embeddings counted separately).
- Model mix baseline: 7B-class 48%, 13B-class 32%, 70B-class 20% of generation workloads. Embeddings offloaded to CPU-backend and excluded from GPU calc.
- GPU throughput (tokens/sec) estimates per full-GPU (serving common seq lengths):
  - A10G (7B fast path): 24,000 tokens/sec
  - A10G (13B): 11,000 tokens/sec
  - A100-80GB (70B): 3,200 tokens/sec
- Effective utilization target for steady-state: 65% (operational), headroom multiplier for bursts: 1.25, maintenance/fallback reserve: 1.10.
- SLO goal: P95 latency < 650ms for interactive routes under baseline.

Input forecast table (CSV format: region,peak-qps,avg-tokens/request,peak-tokens/sec):
us-west,750,240,180000
us-east,420,220,92400
eu-west,220,170,37400
-- note: peak-tokens/sec computed as peak-qps * avg-tokens

Breakdown by model class (global tokens/sec -> GPU estimate):
Global peak tokens/sec by model class (baseline):
- 7B-class: 48% * 360,000 = 172,800 tokens/sec
- 13B-class: 32% * 360,000 = 115,200 tokens/sec
- 70B-class: 20% * 360,000 = 72,000 tokens/sec

GPUs required (raw, before utilization & headroom):
- 7B on A10G: 172,800 / 24,000 = 7.2 -> 8 GPUs
- 13B on A10G: 115,200 / 11,000 = 10.47 -> 11 GPUs
- 70B on A100-80GB: 72,000 / 3,200 = 22.5 -> 23 GPUs
Total raw GPUs: 42 GPUs (by ideal mapping).

Apply utilization & headroom multipliers: effective multiplier = 1 / 0.65 * 1.25 * 1.10 = 2.115 (rounded).
Adjusted GPU requirement (rounded up where needed):
- 7B (A10G): 8 * 2.115 = 17.0 -> 18 GPUs
- 13B (A10G): 11 * 2.115 = 23.3 -> 24 GPUs
- 70B (A100): 23 * 2.115 = 48.6 -> 50 GPUs
Adjusted total: 92 GPUs.

Regional allocation (recommended committed mix) - rationale: keep majority of 70B capacity in us-west and us-east for latency sensitive customers; maintain eu-west with smaller footprint and cross-region failover.
CSV: region,7B-A10G,13B-A10G,70B-A100,total-gpus
us-west,8,10,30,48
us-east,6,8,14,28
eu-west,4,6,6,16
Total,18,24,50,92

Scaling policy & reserved commit recommendation:
- Commit 80 GPUs as Reserved (Reserved = Dedicated capacity contract): prioritize A10G pool first (target 42 A10G reserved) and 38 A100 reserved in us-west/us-east split.
- Keep remaining 12 GPUs as burstable on Hosted autoscale (spot-like capacity) to cover >95th-percentile multi-minute spikes.
- Autoscaler thresholds: scale-up when per-GPU utilization > 70% sustained 30s; scale down when < 40% for 120s. Cooldown: 90s.
- Fast-failover routing: if a region loses >20% of capacity, route to nearest region with available burst pool; embargo non-critical long-generation routes during cross-region fallbacks.

Cost vs reliability tradeoffs (short notes):
- Converting 70B traffic to 13B (via distillation/quantized proxy) reduces A100 need by ~3x at some quality cost; recommended as runbook mitigation during capacity crunches.
- Reserving too many A100s is expensive; hybrid commit with modest A100 reserved + burstable spot A100s recommended for Q1.

Scenario sensitivity (one-line implications):
- +50% tokens/sec growth -> GPUs required ~138 (2x baseline adjusted).
- Model mix shift 40% -> 70B -> GPUs required increases by ~1.6x from adjusted total.
- Longer avg tokens/request (+30%) -> linear increase in tokens/sec and GPU count.

Operational runbook (brief):
- Pre-peak ramp: 45m before daily expected peak, pre-warm 20% of burst pool in each region. Owner: Diego.
- During sustained spike >1.5x baseline for >5m: increase committed burst allocation and enable embargo policy. Owner: Priya.
- Post-incident: run SLA impact report and Model-usage breakdown. Owner: Maya.

Open action items:
- [ ] Confirm A100 spot availability estimates with cloud partners (Due: 2026-03-18) -> Owner: Liam
- [ ] Validate per-route avg tokens from telemetry (sample last 30 days) and update token assumptions (Due: 2026-03-12) -> Owner: Diego
- [ ] Run a controlled failover test us-west -> us-east during low traffic window (Due: 2026-03-25) -> Owner: Priya

Notes and caveats:
- Throughput numbers are modeled for common sequence lengths; very long sequences (>=2k tokens) degrade throughput non-linearly and will require separate sizing.
- Embeddings and CPU-offloaded workloads not included here — separate sheet handles CPU & memory capacity.
- This doc is a working draft intended for review with Product and Solutions Eng prior to finalizing Reserved commitments.

History/edits:
- 2026-02-20 Maya Chen: initial draft and baseline numbers.
- 2026-03-10 Diego Ramirez: updated regional QPS and corrected A100 throughput estimate.
